💔 How to Cancel Your Subscription

To stop your recurring billing with Blueberry Futures, follow these four simple steps in your dashboard.

November 24, 2025
Step-by-Step Cancellation Process

Log In to Your Account: Access your Blueberry Futures trader dashboard.

Navigate to 'Account': Find the 'Subscriptions' tab on the Superior menu.

Select 'Cancel Subscription': Click the option to manage your current plan details.

Confirm Cancellation: A final prompt will appear asking you to confirm your decision. Click 'Yes' to finalize the cancellation.

 

 

Important Considerations

Account Access: Your trading account remains active and accessible until the end of the current paid billing cycle.

Challenge Reset: Canceled Evaluation are immediately ineligible for any future resets, even if the cancellation is future-dated.

Payouts: Ensure all pending payouts have been processed before your access ends.

 

 

Note: If you are experiencing difficulties or would like to provide feedback, please contact our support team before canceling.

Drawdown Types: EOD vs. Trailing Explained
November 24, 2025

Understanding how your maximum loss limit is calculated is the single most important rule for passing your challenge. Blueberry Futures offers two distinct drawdown models to suit different trading styles: End-of-Day (EOD) Drawdown and Real-Time Trailing Drawdown.

 

Accelerated Challenge: Trailing Drawdown

The Trailing Drawdown is a dynamic loss limit that tracks your account's peak value in real-time throughout the trading day.

 

How it Works:
Dynamic Limit

The Drawdown Limit follows your highest live account equity (this includes both closed profits and unrealized profits from open positions).
​

The Rule

Your Trailing Drawdown Limit is always your maximum allowed loss amount (e.g., $2,000 for the $50K plan) subtracted from your highest peak equity.

 

Current Limit = Highest Peak Equity - Max Drawdown Amount
​
Movement

When your account makes new equity highs, the Drawdown Limit moves up accordingly.

 

Lock-in

Once the limit moves up, it never moves back down, even if your account equity falls. It is locked in at the highest point achieved, protecting the firm's capital.

 

Breach

If your live account equity drops below the most recently adjusted Trailing Drawdown Limit at any point during the trading day, your challenge is failed.

 

Trailing Example:

Trailing Drawdown Example 

(50K Plan with $2,000 Max Drawdown)

$50,000




Initial Drawdown Limit

	

$48,000




Equity Peak

	

$51,000 (Achieved intra-day)




New Drawdown Limit

	

$49,000 (Locked in at $51,000 - $2,000)$




Account Fails If...

	

Equity drops below $49,000

 

Ascent Challenge: End-of-Day (EOD) Drawdown

The EOD Drawdown is a loss limit that only updates when the trading session is officially closed. This gives traders more room to manage intra-day volatility.
​ 

How it Works:
End-of-Day Limit

The Drawdown Limit is calculated only from your end-of-day closed balance. On days you finish in profit, your minimum required balance trails upward; on flat or losing days, it stays the same.

 

Updates

The minimum balance is only adjusted at the end of the trading day and is always based on closed profits, not intraday spikes. Unrealized (floating) profits during the day do not move the drawdown.

 

The Rule

Current Minimum Balance = Highest End-of-Day Closing Balance Reached So Far − Max Drawdown Amount

 

Intraday Risk

Although the limit only recalculates once per day after the session closes, your live equity (including open positions) must never fall below the current Minimum Balance at any time. If it does, the challenge is breached.
​

Trader Advantage: Because the limit only moves at end-of-day and does not follow intraday peaks, you can experience larger intraday pullbacks from your peak equity without breaching, as long as your equity never falls below the current Minimum Balance.

Explains the maximum number of mini and micro contracts each account size can hold, and how the system enforces these limits.

December 21, 2025

To keep risk controlled and account behavior consistent, each Blueberry Futures account size has a built-in cap on how many contracts you can hold at one time.

These limits are enforced by the platform, so if you try to exceed them, your order will be rejected or not fully accepted. You won’t be able to open more than the allowed size.

Contract Limits by Account Size

$25,000 account

Max 1 Mini Contract

Max 10 Micro Contracts

$50,000 account

Max 2 mini contracts

Max 20 micro contracts

$100,000 account

Max 6 mini contracts

Max 60 micro contracts

$150,000 account

Max 9 mini contracts

Max 90 micro contracts

These caps apply to your net open exposure on that account.
The system continuously checks your open positions and prevents you from going beyond these limits.

What this means in practice

If you are at your max size and try to add more contracts, the platform will block the extra size.

You may still scale in (DCA) within these limits, as long as:

Your total contracts stay under the cap, and

You respect the separate DCA & Position Stacking rule (max 3 entries per instrument/direction).

Examples

50K account – minis

You open 2 ES minis → system allows it.

You try to buy a 3rd ES mini → system will not allow you to exceed 2 minis.

100K account – micros

You build up to 90 total micros on allowed instruments → system allows it.

You try to add more micros beyond that → extra size is blocked.

Relationship to the DCA & Position Stacking Rule

The Max Contracts limits are enforced automatically by the system.
However, the DCA & Position Stacking rule is a behavior rule, not a hard platform cap:

You can only enter the same instrument and direction up to 3 times (1 initial entry + 2 adds), even if the system would technically let you click more.

For details on that behavior rule, see:

DCA & Position Stacking Limits.

Are there limits on DCA? (Stacking)

🧱 Yes. You may stack a maximum of 3 positions per trade idea.

DCA & Position Stacking Limits

We allow you to scale into trades (Dollar Cost Averaging), but we also limit how many times you can “stack” into the same idea. This keeps trading behavior controlled and prevents excessive, high-frequency averaging down.

 

This is a behavior rule that applies independently of account size.

 

The DCA / Stacking Rule

You may enter the same instrument, same direction up to 3 times total for a single trade idea:

1 initial entry

Up to 2 additional adds (DCA entries)
​

This 3-entry limit is the same for:

$50,000 accounts

$100,000 accounts

$150,000 accounts

Even if your total contracts are under your Max Contracts limit, a 4th entry into the same instrument/direction for the same idea is considered stacking behavior and is not allowed.
​

Examples
Example 1 – Rule respected (100K account)

Plan max contracts: 6 minis

Trader does:

Buy 2 ES → add 2 ES → add 2 ES

Result:

3 entries total, 6 minis → ✅ Within DCA rule and ✅ within max contracts

Example 2 – DCA behavior violation (any account size)

Trader does:

Buy 1 ES → add 1 ES → add 1 ES → add 1 ES

Result:

4 separate entries in the same direction on ES → ❌ violates DCA rule, even if total minis are still under the contract cap

Example 3 – Contract violation despite OK DCA (50K account)

50K account max: 2 minis

Trader does:

Buy 1 ES → add 1 ES → add 1 ES

Result:

3 entries (OK for DCA), but 3 minis open when the max allowed is 2 → ❌ breaches Max Contracts rule

Why this rule exists

The 3-entry limit is there to:

Prevent uncontrolled “spray and pray” averaging behavior

Keep trade data cleaner and more consistent for risk management

Still allow planned scaling in without turning trades into a grid/martingale pattern

You must always respect both:

DCA & Position Stacking Limits (max 3 entries per idea), and

Max Contracts by Account Size (2 / 6 / 9 minis or 20 / 60 / 60 micros).

Can I use EAs, Bots, or Copy Trading?

Automated trading software is allowed on Blueberry Futures only if it is proprietary, runs your own strategy, and has been disclosed to us with consent received before you run it. Commercial and third-party systems are not allowed.

October 1, 2026

 

You can use automated trading software on your Blueberry Futures account only if it meets all three of these conditions:

It is proprietary. You built it yourself. Not bought, rented, shared, or commissioned from someone else.

It runs your own strategy. The trading logic and risk decisions in it are yours.

You disclosed it and received our consent before running it. Contact support, tell us what the tool is and what it does, and wait for our confirmation before it places a single trade.

This applies on every account and at every stage.

 

 

What's allowed

Automated strategies you built yourself, running your own logic, disclosed and approved before use. You must be able to demonstrate that you own the source code.

Risk and execution tools that assist with trades you decide on, such as position sizers, risk calculators and partial-close managers.

Copying your own trades between your own Blueberry Futures accounts.

 

What's not allowed

Commercial or commercial-license systems, whether paid or free. Being able to change the settings does not make one yours.

Systems built for you by a developer, freelancer or third party on commission.

Systems obtained from a friend, a Discord group, a signal group or a marketplace.

Any automated system run without disclosing it and receiving our consent first, including one you built yourself.

Signal copying. Mirroring trades from an external signal provider or copytrading service.

Third-party account management. Letting anyone else trade your account, including granting login access.

 

 

Why the line is drawn here

We fund traders, not software vendors. A system you built around your own strategy is your skill, automated, and we support that. A system someone else built, sold, or runs on your behalf is not your edge, so it falls outside what we allow.

 

 

How to get consent

Contact our support team before you run anything automated. Tell us what the tool is, what it does, and confirm you own the source code. Running automated execution without prior consent can put your account and payouts at risk.

What is the Consistency Rule?
What is the Consistency Rule?

📉 We fund consistent traders. Learn about the 20% (Accelerated) and 35% (Ascent) profit rules.

August 3, 2026
Why we have a Consistency Rule

To make sure you're using a sustainable strategy, and not just getting lucky on one massive trade, we enforce a Consistency Rule on all Funded Accounts. The specific percentage depends on the account type you chose.
​

The Rule

No single trading day can account for more than a set percentage of your total profit at the time of a withdrawal request.

Account Type

	

Max Profit per Day




🚀 Accelerated

	

20% of Total Profit




🏔️ Ascent

	

35% of Total Profit

How to read your Consistency figure on the dashboard

Your dashboard shows a Consistency percentage. It represents your largest single trading day as a proportion of your total profit:

Consistency % = (Largest single-day profit ÷ Total profit) × 100

To be eligible for a withdrawal, this figure must be at or below your account's limit (20% for Accelerated, 35% for Ascent).

Largest day under the limit → ✅ you pass the consistency test.

Largest day over the limit → ❌ keep trading to grow your total profit until that day represents a smaller share.

⏰ Important: Time Zones, why your numbers might not match the dashboard

This is the single most common reason a trader's own math disagrees with the dashboard. Please read this before assuming there's a calculation bug.

Your trades on BlackArrow are displayed in UTC. But every Challenge calculation, including the Consistency Rule, is measured in CST, the Challenge Time Zone configured for your account.
​

Why that matters:

A trading "day" runs from midnight to midnight.

CST (US Central Time) is behind UTC by roughly 5–6 hours (depending on daylight saving).

So a trade placed close to midnight can land on one calendar day in UTC but a different calendar day in CST.

When trades shift between days, the profit attributed to each day changes, which changes your largest day, your totals, and therefore your consistency figure.

Example: Two sessions that look like two separate days in UTC may actually fall on the same day in CST, combining into a single, larger day. That one larger day can raise your consistency percentage even though your total profit hasn't changed at all.
​

✅ Always evaluate your consistency using the CST view. That's the time zone the rule is enforced on. If you calculate from the UTC / BlackArrow view, your numbers can look different from the dashboard even when nothing is wrong, and any manual correction based on UTC won't "stick," because the system always recalculates on CST.

🔄 How to switch your view from UTC to CST

 

To check your figures the same way the system does:

Open your Dashboard (or the trades view in BlackArrow).

Locate the time-zone toggle (Top Right corner of the PnL Day Calendar).
​
​


​

Switch the view from UTC to CST.

Re-check your daily profit breakdown and your largest single day, these now match how the Consistency Rule is calculated.

Tip: If your dashboard consistency figure ever looks "impossible" compared with your own math, switch to CST first and recompute. The discrepancy almost always disappears.

Worked examples

Withdrawal minimums ($100k account): To request a withdrawal on a $100k account, you must have at least $3,850 in profit (the $3,100 buffer + $750 minimum withdrawal).
​

Scenario 1 — Accelerated Trader (20% rule)

Total profit: $4,000

The limit: $4,000 × 20% = $800

Best day (CST): $1,500

$1,500 is greater than $800 → Withdrawal denied. Continue trading until that $1,500 day is less than 20% of your total.

Scenario 2 — Ascent Trader (35% rule)

Total profit: $4,000

The limit: $4,000 × 35% = $1,400

Best day (CST): $1,500

$1,500 is still slightly above $1,400 → Withdrawal denied, but you're much closer than the Accelerated trader.

How to become eligible

If your largest day is over the limit, you have two levers:

Grow your total profit. As your total rises, your largest day becomes a smaller share of it. To find the total profit you need, divide your largest day by the limit: Largest day ÷ limit %.

Example (Ascent, 35%): an $1,855 largest day needs $1,855 ÷ 0.35 = $5,300 in total profit before that day is within range.

Keep future days balanced. Avoid concentrating profit in one outsized session.

Quick FAQ

My manual calculation doesn't match the dashboard. Is it a bug? Almost always this is the UTC vs CST difference explained above. Switch to the CST view and recompute, the rule is enforced on CST.
​

My consistency figure changed to a different number and then reverted. Why? Temporary or manual values based on UTC won't hold, because the system recalculates on CST. The CST figure is the one that governs withdrawals.
​

Which number counts for my withdrawal? The CST consistency figure shown on your dashboard at the time you submit the withdrawal request.

The payout cycle at Blueberry Futures is designed to reward consistent performance. 

 

To request a withdrawal, you must meet specific trading conditions, consistency rules, and profit thresholds.

 

1. Eligibility Requirements

Before a payout button becomes available, you must meet ALL of the following criteria within the current cycle:

Active Trading: You must have traded at least 5 profitable days.

Profitable Day Definition: A day is only counted if you generate a net profit of $200 or more. (Days with less than $200 profit do not count).

Consistency Rule: No single day can account for more than a specific % of your total profit.

Accelerated: Max 20% from a single day.

Ascent: Max 35% from a single day.

 

2. Limits & Buffer Rules

You can only withdraw funds that are in excess of your Required Buffer, up to the Maximum Cap.

3. How the Buffer Works (Real-Examples)

Here is exactly how to calculate what you can withdraw based on your total profit.

The Rules: Max Cap ($1,500) | Buffer ($1,100)

Result: You can withdraw $4,400 right now.

To get the full $4,500 max payout, you would need to build your profit to $9,100.

 

4. Account Pause & Reset

Processing: Once you request a payout, your account is temporarily paused (read-only) while we process the funds. You can resume trading immediately after approval.

Cycle Reset: After a payout, your "5 Day Count" resets. You must complete 5 new profitable days, maintain consistency within the new cycle to qualify for the next withdrawal.

Referral Tracking

September 25, 2026

Referrals are tracked using a 180-day cookie window 🍪. When someone clicks your referral link, a cookie is stored in their browser. If they make a purchase any time within those 180 days, the sale is credited to you, and you'll keep earning commission on their repeat purchases too. 
​

What the cookie window means

You don't need an instant sale. A visitor can click your link today and buy weeks later, as long as it's within 180 days, you still get the credit.

Repeat purchases count. Once someone is attributed to you, future purchases from that client continue to earn you commission, not just their first order.

Tracking with a discount code
If you use a custom discount code (the 10% OFF code for your audience), sales made with that code are tracked to you as well. Codes are a reliable backup to link tracking, since they still attribute the sale even if a customer's browser doesn't retain the cookie.
​

Things that can affect tracking
Cookie-based tracking depends on the customer's browser, so a few situations can interrupt it:

Clearing cookies or browsing in private/incognito mode before purchasing

Clicking your link on one device but buying on another

Browser or ad-blocker settings that block tracking cookies

Sharing your custom discount code alongside your link is the best way to keep attribution solid in these cases.

What is the Consistency Rule?

📉 We fund consistent traders. Learn about the 20% (Accelerated) and 35% (Ascent) profit rules.

August 3, 2026
Why we have a Consistency Rule

To make sure you're using a sustainable strategy, and not just getting lucky on one massive trade, we enforce a Consistency Rule on all Funded Accounts. The specific percentage depends on the account type you chose.
​

The Rule

No single trading day can account for more than a set percentage of your total profit at the time of a withdrawal request.

Account Type

	

Max Profit per Day




🚀 Accelerated

	

20% of Total Profit




🏔️ Ascent

	

35% of Total Profit

How to read your Consistency figure on the dashboard

Your dashboard shows a Consistency percentage. It represents your largest single trading day as a proportion of your total profit:

Consistency % = (Largest single-day profit ÷ Total profit) × 100

To be eligible for a withdrawal, this figure must be at or below your account's limit (20% for Accelerated, 35% for Ascent).

Largest day under the limit → ✅ you pass the consistency test.

Largest day over the limit → ❌ keep trading to grow your total profit until that day represents a smaller share.

⏰ Important: Time Zones, why your numbers might not match the dashboard

This is the single most common reason a trader's own math disagrees with the dashboard. Please read this before assuming there's a calculation bug.

Your trades on BlackArrow are displayed in UTC. But every Challenge calculation, including the Consistency Rule, is measured in CST, the Challenge Time Zone configured for your account.
​

Why that matters:

A trading "day" runs from midnight to midnight.

CST (US Central Time) is behind UTC by roughly 5–6 hours (depending on daylight saving).

So a trade placed close to midnight can land on one calendar day in UTC but a different calendar day in CST.

When trades shift between days, the profit attributed to each day changes, which changes your largest day, your totals, and therefore your consistency figure.

Example: Two sessions that look like two separate days in UTC may actually fall on the same day in CST, combining into a single, larger day. That one larger day can raise your consistency percentage even though your total profit hasn't changed at all.
​

✅ Always evaluate your consistency using the CST view. That's the time zone the rule is enforced on. If you calculate from the UTC / BlackArrow view, your numbers can look different from the dashboard even when nothing is wrong, and any manual correction based on UTC won't "stick," because the system always recalculates on CST.

🔄 How to switch your view from UTC to CST

 

To check your figures the same way the system does:

Open your Dashboard (or the trades view in BlackArrow).

Locate the time-zone toggle (Top Right corner of the PnL Day Calendar).
​
​


​

Switch the view from UTC to CST.

Re-check your daily profit breakdown and your largest single day, these now match how the Consistency Rule is calculated.

Tip: If your dashboard consistency figure ever looks "impossible" compared with your own math, switch to CST first and recompute. The discrepancy almost always disappears.

Worked examples

Withdrawal minimums ($100k account): To request a withdrawal on a $100k account, you must have at least $3,850 in profit (the $3,100 buffer + $750 minimum withdrawal).
​

Scenario 1 — Accelerated Trader (20% rule)

Total profit: $4,000

The limit: $4,000 × 20% = $800

Best day (CST): $1,500

$1,500 is greater than $800 → Withdrawal denied. Continue trading until that $1,500 day is less than 20% of your total.

Scenario 2 — Ascent Trader (35% rule)

Total profit: $4,000

The limit: $4,000 × 35% = $1,400

Best day (CST): $1,500

$1,500 is still slightly above $1,400 → Withdrawal denied, but you're much closer than the Accelerated trader.

How to become eligible

If your largest day is over the limit, you have two levers:

Grow your total profit. As your total rises, your largest day becomes a smaller share of it. To find the total profit you need, divide your largest day by the limit: Largest day ÷ limit %.

Example (Ascent, 35%): an $1,855 largest day needs $1,855 ÷ 0.35 = $5,300 in total profit before that day is within range.

Keep future days balanced. Avoid concentrating profit in one outsized session.

Quick FAQ

My manual calculation doesn't match the dashboard. Is it a bug? Almost always this is the UTC vs CST difference explained above. Switch to the CST view and recompute, the rule is enforced on CST.
​

My consistency figure changed to a different number and then reverted. Why? Temporary or manual values based on UTC won't hold, because the system recalculates on CST. The CST figure is the one that governs withdrawals.
​

Which number counts for my withdrawal? The CST consistency figure shown on your dashboard at the time you submit the withdrawal request.

July 13, 2026

Dissatisfaction with challenge rules or trading conditions

Failure to trade or use the account after purchase

Payments made via any method other than a direct debit or credit card transaction, including but not limited to: Apple Pay, Google Pay, and other mobile wallets; PayPal; Skrill; UPI; cryptocurrency; bank transfers; and any other third-party or alternative payment method

Payments sent via an incorrect or unsupported crypto network

Partially completed challenges or breached accounts

Exceptions

For payments made by direct debit/credit card only (excluding mobile wallets such as Apple Pay and Google Pay, and all other alternative payment methods), a refund request will only be reviewed in the following situations:

Duplicate or accidental purchase - where the same order was charged more than once, supported by payment evidence

Service non-delivery - where Blueberry Futures is unable to provide account access after confirmed support attempts within our resolution timeframe

Your order number

Your account ID

The email address used at checkout

Requests submitted outside the 14-day window or without the required details will not be processed.

Promotional Refunds

Cancelling Your Account

To cancel your account, shoot us an email at support@blueberryfutures.com.

After cancellation, all access to your account and Blueberry Futures services will be revoked. No refunds will be issued for previously paid fees.

Right to Termination

Deactivating accounts

Drawdown Types: EOD vs. Trailing Explained
November 24, 2025

Understanding how your maximum loss limit is calculated is the single most important rule for passing your challenge. Blueberry Futures offers two distinct drawdown models to suit different trading styles: End-of-Day (EOD) Drawdown and Real-Time Trailing Drawdown.

 

Accelerated Challenge: Trailing Drawdown

The Trailing Drawdown is a dynamic loss limit that tracks your account's peak value in real-time throughout the trading day.

 

How it Works:
Dynamic Limit

The Drawdown Limit follows your highest live account equity (this includes both closed profits and unrealized profits from open positions).
​

The Rule

Your Trailing Drawdown Limit is always your maximum allowed loss amount (e.g., $2,000 for the $50K plan) subtracted from your highest peak equity.

 

Current Limit = Highest Peak Equity - Max Drawdown Amount
​
Movement

When your account makes new equity highs, the Drawdown Limit moves up accordingly.

 

Lock-in

Once the limit moves up, it never moves back down, even if your account equity falls. It is locked in at the highest point achieved, protecting the firm's capital.

 

Breach

If your live account equity drops below the most recently adjusted Trailing Drawdown Limit at any point during the trading day, your challenge is failed.

Ascent Challenge: End-of-Day (EOD) Drawdown

The EOD Drawdown is a loss limit that only updates when the trading session is officially closed. This gives traders more room to manage intra-day volatility.
​ 

How it Works:
End-of-Day Limit

The Drawdown Limit is calculated only from your end-of-day closed balance. On days you finish in profit, your minimum required balance trails upward; on flat or losing days, it stays the same.

 

Updates

The minimum balance is only adjusted at the end of the trading day and is always based on closed profits, not intraday spikes. Unrealized (floating) profits during the day do not move the drawdown.

 

The Rule

Current Minimum Balance = Highest End-of-Day Closing Balance Reached So Far − Max Drawdown Amount

 

Intraday Risk

Although the limit only recalculates once per day after the session closes, your live equity (including open positions) must never fall below the current Minimum Balance at any time. If it does, the challenge is breached.
​

Trader Advantage: Because the limit only moves at end-of-day and does not follow intraday peaks, you can experience larger intraday pullbacks from your peak equity without breaching, as long as your equity never falls below the current Minimum Balance.

To keep risk controlled and account behavior consistent, each Blueberry Futures account size has a built-in cap on how many contracts you can hold at one time.

These limits are enforced by the platform, so if you try to exceed them, your order will be rejected or not fully accepted. You won’t be able to open more than the allowed size.

Max 60 micro contracts

These caps apply to your net open exposure on that account.
The system continuously checks your open positions and prevents you from going beyond these limits.

What this means in practice

If you are at your max size and try to add more contracts, the platform will block the extra size.

Your total contracts stay under the cap, and

Relationship to the DCA & Position Stacking Rule

The Max Contracts limits are enforced automatically by the system.

You can only enter the same instrument and direction up to 3 times (1 initial entry + 2 adds), even if the system would technically let you click more.

You cannot execute new trades 3 minutes before and 3 minutes after a Red Folder (High Impact) news event on the affected asset.

Closures: You may manually close trades to lock in profit or prevent loss at any time.

Consequence

Profits made from opening new trades during the restricted window will be deducted. Repeated violations will lead to an account review.

Are there limits on DCA? (Stacking)

🧱 Yes. You may stack a maximum of 3 positions per trade idea.

November 24, 2025
DCA & Position Stacking Limits

We allow you to scale into trades (Dollar Cost Averaging), but we also limit how many times you can “stack” into the same idea. This keeps trading behavior controlled and prevents excessive, high-frequency averaging down.

 

This is a behavior rule that applies independently of account size.

 

The DCA / Stacking Rule

You may enter the same instrument, same direction up to 3 times total for a single trade idea:

1 initial entry

Up to 2 additional adds (DCA entries)
​

This 3-entry limit is the same for:

$50,000 accounts

$100,000 accounts

$150,000 accounts

Even if your total contracts are under your Max Contracts limit, a 4th entry into the same instrument/direction for the same idea is considered stacking behavior and is not allowed.
​

Examples
Example 1 – Rule respected (100K account)

Plan max contracts: 6 minis

Trader does:

Buy 2 ES → add 2 ES → add 2 ES

Result:

3 entries total, 6 minis → ✅ Within DCA rule and ✅ within max contracts

Example 2 – DCA behavior violation (any account size)

Trader does:

Buy 1 ES → add 1 ES → add 1 ES → add 1 ES

Result:

4 separate entries in the same direction on ES → ❌ violates DCA rule, even if total minis are still under the contract cap

Example 3 – Contract violation despite OK DCA (50K account)

50K account max: 2 minis

Trader does:

Buy 1 ES → add 1 ES → add 1 ES

Result:

3 entries (OK for DCA), but 3 minis open when the max allowed is 2 → ❌ breaches Max Contracts rule

Why this rule exists

The 3-entry limit is there to:

Prevent uncontrolled “spray and pray” averaging behavior

Keep trade data cleaner and more consistent for risk management

Still allow planned scaling in without turning trades into a grid/martingale pattern

You must always respect both:

DCA & Position Stacking Limits (max 3 entries per idea), and

Max Contracts by Account Size (2 / 6 / 9 minis or 20 / 60 / 60 micros).

Scalping & Minimum Position Time

If you are manually entering and exiting trades based on market structure, you have nothing to worry about. Legitimate scalping typically lasts significantly longer than the latency of a data feed.

Referrals are tracked using a 180-day cookie window 🍪. When someone clicks your referral link, a cookie is stored in their browser. If they make a purchase any time within those 180 days, the sale is credited to you, and you'll keep earning commission on their repeat purchases too.

What the cookie window means

You don't need an instant sale. A visitor can click your link today and buy weeks later, as long as it's within 180 days, you still get the credit.

Tracking with a discount code
If you use a custom discount code (the 10% OFF code for your audience), sales made with that code are tracked to you as well. Codes are a reliable backup to link tracking, since they still attribute the sale even if a customer's browser doesn't retain the cookie.
​

Things that can affect tracking
Cookie-based tracking depends on the customer's browser, so a few situations can interrupt it:

Clearing cookies or browsing in private/incognito mode before purchasing

Clicking your link on one device but buying on another

Browser or ad-blocker settings that block tracking cookies

Sharing your custom discount code alongside your link is the best way to keep attribution solid in these cases.

Affiliate payouts are processed every Friday via Riseworks. Once your affiliate balance reaches the $200 minimum, you can request a withdrawal from your affiliate Blueberry Futures dashboard. Here's the full process: 
​

1. Build up your balance
Every eligible commission from your referrals is added to your affiliate balance. Only commissions from completed, retained sales count toward your withdrawable total. If a referred user cancels or is refunded, that commission is voided or deducted.
​

2. Reach the $200 minimum
You can submit a withdrawal request once your balance reaches $200. If you're below the threshold, your balance simply carries over and keeps building until you get there; nothing is lost.
​

3. Submit your request in your dashboard
Go to the Affiliate Dashboard in your Blueberry Futures dashboard and submit a withdrawal request for your available balance.
​

4. Get paid every Friday via Riseworks
Payouts run on a weekly cycle every Friday through Riseworks, our payments partner. To receive funds, make sure your Riseworks account is set up, and your details are verified (a one-time step for first-time affiliates).

Is there a minimum number of referrals needed to remain active?

Minimum Referrals

September 25, 2026

No, there's no minimum referral requirement to stay in the affiliate program. Whether you refer one person or hundreds, your account stays active and your referral link keeps working.
​

The only threshold that applies is for payouts:
​

The $200 payout minimum
​
You can request a withdrawal once your affiliate balance reaches $200 USD. This isn't a condition for staying in the program, it just means commissions below $200 remain in your balance and keep building until you reach the threshold. Nothing is lost while you get there.
​

Your referral count doesn't affect your status — but it does affect your rate
There's no minimum to remain active, but the total number of referrals you generate determines your commission tier:

Tier 1: 15% (0–20 referrals)

Tier 2: 18% (20–100 referrals)

Tier 3: 20% (100+ referrals)

So more referrals mean a higher commission rate, but even at zero referrals, your account stays open and ready.
